text:
# Minimum hardening deployment and recovery

This release keeps Dodo in test mode and Gmail send-only. It adds no mailbox reads,
bounce detection, automated responses or resend of ambiguous submissions. It does
not enable real payments or provision backups.

## Deploy

1. Back up the database and preserve the existing legacy `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
   Inventory backup/PITR and rollback retention; the actual retention policy
   is a deployment input.
2. Disable checkout and pause sending using existing operator controls. Drain and
   stop old workers before configuring v2 writes. Keep webhook reception and billing
   recovery running. All active processes must support v1/v2 decryption, including
   Auth.js, deletion workers and maintenance.
3. Run `npm run db:generate` and `npm run db:deploy`. The additive migration is
   `20261020050000_minimum_hardening`; do not remove historical billing buckets,
   reservations, pause state, receipts or financial records.
4. New operator roles use `scripts/provision-admin-db.ts`. For an existing role,
   run `npx tsx scripts/provision-admin-db.ts --upgrade-hardening` with the owner
   `DATABASE_URL` and restricted `ADMIN_DATABASE_URL`. This grants only SELECT,
   INSERT and UPDATE on the content-free `RateLimitBucket` table. Re-run restricted
   role privacy checks; never grant access to tokens, recipients or email content.
5. Configure the active key ID/key and prior-key map below.
6. Stop old workers and deploy the updated Inngest endpoint. Remove
   `minimum-hardening-monitor` and `operator-alert-delivery` registrations. Verify
   `rate-limit-cleanup` runs daily at 04:00 UTC (`0 4 * * *`). Preserve quota
   reconciliation and billing recovery. Verify `account-deletion-jobs` runs daily
   at 02:00 UTC (`0 2 * * *`), and `deletion-maintenance` is absent.
7. Apply `20261021000000_remove_operator_alerts` after stopping old code. This
   removes the alert outbox and deletion-alert bookkeeping. Preserve financial,
   delivery, pause and deletion-recovery records. The operator webhook environment
   variables are no longer used.
8. Check safe error logs and persisted retry/deletion state manually. Automatic
   operator notifications, scans and the minute heartbeat have been removed.
9. Complete the backup/key recovery exercise below before calling hardening ready.

## Limits and failure behavior

All limits are strict rolling windows using database time, per-budget row locks,
and bounded timestamp arrays. Authentication precedes admission. Admission commits
before parsing and business transactions; failed requests and idempotent replays
consume capacity. Database/limiter failure blocks the operation with 503 or action
code `UNAVAILABLE`. Denial returns HTTP 429 plus `Retry-After`, or action code
`RATE_LIMITED` and `retryAfter` seconds.

| Operation                           | Budget                                      |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Checkout                            | 5 / 10 minutes / owner                      |
| Portal + cancel combined            | 10 / minute / owner                         |
| Billing status                      | 30 / minute / owner                         |
| Campaign submission                 | 10 / minute / owner                         |
| CSV import                          | 5 / hour / owner                            |
| Account + template exports combined | 2 / hour / owner                            |
| Admin mutations                     | 20 / minute / actor                         |
| System controls, additionally       | 5 / minute / actor and 10 / minute globally |

Admin budgets are admitted atomically in stable lock order. Provider callbacks and
recovery jobs consume no user budget. Suspended users retain billing management.
Expired limiter rows are deleted daily in batches of 500, up to 10,000 per run,
without blocking active budgets. Only rows whose `cleanupAt` is more than one day
old qualify; excess or locked rows wait for a later pass. Request-time expiry is
independent of this cleanup.

Logs validate fixed event codes, UUIDs, timestamps,
bounded counts and outcome booleans. Raw provider payloads, nested errors, headers,
URLs, addresses, subjects, bodies and credentials are not accepted. Auth.js hooks,
SDK logging and Inngest step/function errors use the same safe boundary. Webhooks
correlate by internal receipt UUID, never by attacker/provider-supplied webhook IDs.

Gmail checks owner/project pauses at publication, preflight and final claim. Provider
calls hold no owner lock. Daily/project limits honor provider deadlines or default
to six hours. Retry-After >=1 hour is a long provider cooldown. Transient throttles pause other queued work for at least one minute.
Each email gets one sending attempt; definite Gmail rejections and preparation
failures finish immediately and release their reservations. The email worker has
automatic retries disabled. A definite 401 or revocation requires reconnection. Credential/domain pauses cancel and release only
READY work. Domain policy needs workspace-admin approval. Authorized reconnection
clears credential/policy pauses, preserves suspension and app quota, and never revives
cancelled work. Send-time network/timeout/5xx, unknown provider outcomes and failed
acceptance persistence remain UNCERTAIN, retain accounting and never auto-resend.

## Keys and rotation

Keep these server-only:

- `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`: the fixed legacy-v1 decrypt key.
- `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_ACTIVE_KEY_ID`: 1–64 letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens.
- `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_ACTIVE_KEY`: a new 32-byte key, encoded as 64 hex characters.
- `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_PREVIOUS_KEYS_JSON`: JSON object mapping prior v2 key IDs to
  their 64-character hex keys; exclude the active ID. The default is `{}`.

Provision keys with the secrets manager. New writes use
`v2.<keyId>.<iv>.<tag>.<ciphertext>` with AES-256-GCM. AAD authenticates the version,
key ID, Gmail credential purpose and owner UUID. A deletion job uses the same owner
and purpose when copying its owner's ciphertext. v2 never falls back to another key.
Malformed configuration, key loss, envelope tampering and owner mismatch fail closed
with constant safe errors.

To rotate A → B, retain A in the previous-key map and switch the active ID/key to B
on every process. Keep the legacy key too. Run:

```sh
npm run tokens:rotate
npm run tokens:rotate -- --apply
# Resume after the last successfully completed owner page:
npm run tokens:rotate -- --apply --after=OWNER_UUID
# Validate that every retained credential decrypts and needs no update:
npm run tokens:rotate
```

The default is genuinely read-only: SELECTs and crypto only, no row updates, leases
or checkpoints. Owner pages cover User credentials and unexpired retained deletion
revocation credentials, including jobs whose User no longer exists. Updates compare
ciphertext and current deletion/expiry state; a concurrent reconnect wins and erased
credentials cannot be restored. Logs contain counts and an owner cursor only. A
nonzero failure count stops the CLI; retain the previous successful cursor, fix key
configuration and resume. Re-run from the beginning after any conflicts; it is
idempotent. Dry run must show zero failures and zero eligible records after rotation.
Do not print plaintext, ciphertext, environment contents or key material.

Before retiring A or the v1 key, verify a restored staging backup can decrypt both
user and deletion-job tokens using the stored old keys. Exercise A → B, mixed
v1/A/B records, resumed rotation, concurrent reconnect/deletion and old-key recovery
with fixture credentials and mocked Google revocation. Record the recovery date,
backup identifier, required key IDs, recovery result and monitoring evidence in your
deployment record. Retain old keys **at least 90 days**, and longer while any backup,
PITR window, retained credential or rollback artifact requires them. Never retire a
key merely because the current live database has no matching rows.

## Rollback

Disable checkout and pause sending. Keep verified webhook reception and billing
recovery running. Roll back only to a release that reads both v1 and v2 and honors
persisted pauses and uncertain delivery. Keep the additive schema and financial,
reservation, delivery and encryption state. To roll back the writer, select the
previous active key and retain every required decrypt key. Never restore plaintext,
rewrite ciphertext back to v1, restore erased credentials or resend ambiguous work.

Repository checks do not certify the deployment's backup retention. Recovery
exercises require the operator's backup inputs before deployment readiness can
be declared.
